A few specifics that might matter:

- Transfer pattern: EU-hosted app with inference calls routed to a mix of hosted and dedicated capacity (EU and UK regions).

Can you confirm:
1) Redwood's preferred SCC module for EU transfers (controller -> processor) and whether the UK requires a different addendum/approach;
2) whether this data profile triggers a DPIA on MediCore's side or if Redwood's controls can be referenced instead;
3) any documentation we can attach to our procurement review (SOC 2 scope, encryption details, subprocessors, etc.).

Thanks — would appreciate a short call if helpful.

Thanks for the heads up, Camila. Quick notes from security/privacy: 

1) Module selection: for the scenario described (MediCore = controller; Redwood = processor) Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) of the EU SCCs is the appropriate baseline. For the UK, apply the UK Addendum that maps to the same Controller->Processor protections (there isn't a separate "Module 2" label in UK docs, but operationally we should mirror Module 2 obligations via the UK Addendum + DPA).

2) DPIA trigger: processing of health data (even pseudonymized genomic markers) is likely a high-risk processing activity in most EU jurisdictions — MediCore should perform a DPIA. Redwood can provide a controls appendix to attach to their DPIA (SOC 2 report sections, encryption, RBAC, retention limits, subprocessors). We should not represent Redwood's controls as a substitute for their DPIA, but we will supply the evidence they need.

3) Contract items to include / highlight:
   - DPA referencing Module 2 / UK Addendum equivalence; explicit subprocessors list + 30-day notice for new subprocessors;
   - Right to audit clause: limited scope (security & compliance evidence review via attestation + on-site only for material issues);
   - Data localization mapping: ensure export routing to non-EU/UK regions is blocked unless covered by SCC + UK Addendum;
   - Security requirements: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, per-token logging and KV cache retention policies documented;
   - Retention & deletion SLA for customer data and KV caches (30/90 day options depending on plan).

4) Operational asks for sales/legal: ask the customer for a simple inventory (schema + residency + flow diagram). If they indicate PHI + identifiable genomic markers, suggest we pre-clear an escalation path with our Privacy Counsel for a scoped DPIA assist offering (we can offer a template and a limited consult).

Attachments to include in reply to customer: redwood-sccs-analysis-20270418.pdf, dpia-guidance-checklist.xlsx, and a short execution checklist.

No showstopper here — Module 2 + UK Addendum mapped + DPA + DPIA by customer should be sufficient. If MediCore insists on Controller->Controller Module 1 (rare), we'll need Legal to evaluate but expect additional negotiation.
